Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap + the model pack attached below. I kept it tight to make procurement/product alignment easier.

High-level recommendation (2 tracks):

1) Conservative (lowest hallucination risk, slightly higher cost): Lumos-13B-int8
   - Rationale: strong instruction tuning for factual grounding, engineered safety layers (constrained decoding + calibrated answer templates).
   - Expected median latency (8k context, 1 GPU p99): ~240ms token-step; end-to-end generation for 300-token summary ~600–850ms depending on prefix caching.
   - Unit cost estimate: ~$0.90 / 1k prompt+completion tokens (hosted config).
   - Best where clinical accuracy is prioritized.

2) Cost/latency-first (good quality, fast): Nimbus-7B-quant
   - Rationale: aggressive quantization for throughput, tuned on summarization prompts. Slightly more prone to factual drift on ambiguous inputs.
   - Expected median latency (8k context, 1 GPU p99): ~120ms token-step; 300-token summary ~350–450ms with prefix cache.
   - Unit cost estimate: ~$0.25 / 1k tokens.
   - Good for higher volume pilot where cost and iteration speed matter.

3) Hybrid fallback path (safety/quality buffer): Atlas-70B-ptq (fallback for edge cases)
   - Rationale: highest overall quality on long-context clinical records, used only for items flagged by model confidence or heuristic rules.
   - Latency & cost: higher — ~1.2s per 300-token summary; ~$3.50 / 1k tokens.
   - Use for occasional re-checks, sampling, or post-edit jobs.

Assets attached: prompt set (concord_demo_promptset_v1.json), benchmark CSV (concord_benchmarks_march28.csv), draft SOW (sow_draft_concord.docx). Links: https://drive.redwood.com/concord/benchmarks/march28 (benchmarks & full eval dashboards) and an internal eval run RDW-CON-2028-03.

Operational notes:
- Suggest starting pilot with Nimbus-7B-quant as default and Lumos-13B-int8 behind a 10% canary for quality sampling. Use prefix/KV cache on patient-level keys to reduce cost.
- We'll surface a small prompt guardrail set (included) and a classification hook you can run against outputs for confidence-based routing to Atlas-70B when flagged.

Next steps (proposed):
- I can share a lightweight evaluation template your clinical reviewers can run (1–2hr exercise).
- Ben will follow-up with rollout/ops notes and a suggested pilot config.
- If procurement is good with the SOW draft, we'll schedule kickoff for April 4.

Do these three tracks match the product team's expectations? Happy to tighten the numbers if you have volume targets.

Thanks —
Aisha

Adding the ops/implementation angle here — a few practical bullets for the pilot that will affect latency/cost numbers: 

- Deployment: provision 1 dedicated T4x instance for Nimbus-7B-quant pilot (predictable e2e latency) and a shared pool for Lumos-13B-int8 canary.
- Batching: enable dynamic batching with max wait 4ms for interactive flows; this preserves p99 latency while improving throughput.
- Caching: prefix-level cache for patient EHR snippets; expected token-savings 15–25% on our benchmark.
- Fallback policy: simple confidence threshold + rule-based detect (dates, numeric hallucination) to route to Atlas-70B-ptq. We can ship this as a small Lambda you host or run via Redwood Private if you prefer.

I'll attach a sample rollout JSON in the drive folder. If you want, we can include a one-off regression check in week 2 where clinical reviewers compare 50 pairs sampled from both models.

—Ben
